Position Summary

The Assistant Manager, Quality & Sales Performance plays a key role in supporting the success of the insurance team by ensuring our clients receive consistent, high-quality advice while employees meet established quality, compliance, sales, and performance expectations.

A significant focus of this role is call monitoring and employee coaching. The Assistant Manager will regularly review client interactions to assess the quality of the customer experience, adherence to regulatory and organizational requirements, and the effectiveness of sales behaviours, including identifying client needs, cross-selling, and introducing additional products and services when appropriate.

The Assistant Manager will also maintain regular performance conversations with employees throughout the year, helping them understand their individual targets, where they currently stand, and what actions are needed to achieve their goals.

Ultimately, this role helps connect individual employee performance with the broader goals of the organization, creating accountability while providing employees with practical coaching and support to be successful.

Key Responsibilities

Quality Assurance & Call Monitoring

* Regularly monitor and review client calls and interactions using established quality assurance standards.

* Evaluate interactions for accuracy, professionalism, client experience, documentation, and adherence to organizational procedures.

* Ensure employees are consistently meeting applicable regulatory, licensing, privacy, disclosure, and compliance requirements.

* Identify trends and recurring opportunities across the team and work with leadership to address potential quality or compliance gaps.

* Maintain clear and consistent documentation of call reviews, coaching discussions, and follow-up actions.

* Provide timely, specific feedback so employees clearly understand what they are doing well and where improvement is required.

Sales Behaviour & Cross-Selling

* Coach employees on effective, needs-based sales conversations that balance strong business results with the best interests of the client.

* Monitor whether employees are consistently identifying opportunities to discuss additional products, coverages, or services that may benefit the client.

* Reinforce expectations around cross-selling and identifying coverage gaps as a natural part of the client conversation.

* Help employees improve their confidence in asking questions, identifying needs, making recommendations, and asking for the business.

* Identify opportunities where additional coaching, training, or product knowledge could improve sales results.

* Reinforce the expectation that strong sales performance and a strong client experience should work together.

Performance Management & Coaching

* Hold regular one-on-one performance conversations with employees throughout the year.

* Ensure employees understand their individual goals and how those goals contribute to overall team and organizational results.

* Review performance against established targets such as sales results, cross-selling, productivity, quality assurance, compliance, and customer experience.

* Use actual performance results and call observations to make coaching conversations specific and actionable.

* Recognize strong performance while addressing performance gaps early rather than waiting until formal mid-year or year-end reviews.

* Work with employees to establish clear actions and follow-up commitments when improvement is required.

* Track progress over time and adjust coaching based on individual employee needs and results.

Supporting Team & Company Performance

* Partner with the Manager to monitor overall team performance and identify areas requiring additional attention.

* Help translate broader organizational objectives into clear expectations for individual employees.

* Regularly review team trends and identify where performance may be ahead of or behind plan.

* Support initiatives designed to increase new business, retention, cross-selling, client satisfaction, quality, and operational effectiveness.

* Share recurring themes from call monitoring and coaching with leadership to help identify opportunities for process improvements or additional training.

* Help create a culture where employees understand their results and take ownership of their performance.

* Support the Manager with performance planning, employee development, recognition, and other leadership responsibilities as required.

What Success Looks Like

A successful Assistant Manager helps create a team where employees are never surprised by where they stand.

Employees should understand their targets, know how they are performing against them, and receive regular coaching on the behaviours that will help them improve.

Success in this role would be demonstrated through:

* Consistent completion of call monitoring and quality reviews

* Strong quality assurance and compliance results

* Increased adoption of needs-based selling and cross-selling behaviours

* Improved conversion and products-per-client results

* Clear and consistent performance coaching

* Early identification and management of performance gaps

* Progress against individual and team sales targets

* Strong client experience and call quality results

* Effective employee development and improved performance over time

* Achievement of broader team and organizational objectives

Qualifications

* Previous experience in insurance, financial services, sales, customer service, or a related environment.

* Previous leadership, coaching, quality assurance, or performance-management experience preferred.

* Strong understanding of insurance sales and service environments.

* Ability to assess client conversations objectively and provide clear, practical feedback.

* Strong coaching skills with the ability to have both positive and challenging performance conversations.

* Comfortable working with sales targets, quality scores, productivity measures, and other performance metrics.

* Strong understanding of the importance of regulatory compliance and appropriate needs-based insurance conversations.

* Excellent communication and relationship-building skills.

* Strong organizational skills and ability to maintain a consistent coaching and call-monitoring schedule.

* Ability to identify patterns in performance data and translate them into practical coaching opportunities.

Ideal Candidate

You are a hands-on leader who enjoys developing people and improving performance.

You are comfortable listening to a client conversation and identifying both the positives and the missed opportunities. You can recognize when an employee delivered an excellent client experience but could have asked one more question, uncovered an additional need, or introduced another relevant product.

You are equally comfortable addressing situations where quality or compliance expectations have not been met.

Most importantly, you believe employees perform best when expectations are clear, feedback is regular, and there is open communication about results. You don't wait for a formal performance review to tell someone how they're doing. You have those conversations consistently throughout the year and help employees understand what they can do differently to achieve their goals.

Leadership Approach

The Assistant Manager should bring a coaching-first approach with clear accountability.

The goal isn't simply to monitor calls or report numbers. It's to use those insights to help employees improve. That means connecting the dots between what happens on a client call, an employee's individual results, the quality of advice we're providing, and the overall performance of the business.

**About Compass International Holdings**

Compass International Holdings is the largest residential real estate brokerage in the United States by sales volume. Technology is not a support function here; it is the product that differentiates the company. That is what makes infrastructure a first-class concern — and it is the premise of this role. Just as Compass makes agents more effective, Technical Infrastructure exists to make our Product and Engineering teams more effective.

**About the Role**

As Director of Engineering for Technical Infrastructure, you will own the platform that every engineer at Compass builds on. Tech Infra's mission is to empower our engineers to build, test, and ship high-quality software with maximum speed and confidence by providing a reliable, cost-effective "Golden Path" of centralized tools that eliminates operational complexity so product teams can focus on innovation. You will be accountable for that mission across compute, networking, databases, streaming, build and release systems, test infrastructure, observability, developer tooling, and the AI-enabled software development lifecycle. You will support a footprint that today spans more than 1,400 services, hundreds of managed datastores, and thousands of engineers' daily workflows.

This is a manager-of-managers role in a functional area with an expectation to shape the infrastructure architecture and technology strategy for years to come. You will own a domain where the business problem is not always defined for you and the technology strategy could be genuinely open — where part of the job is determining what the right problem is before committing the organization to solving it. You will set the high-level vision and long-term direction, make the case for resourcing initiatives that span multiple years, and take on the endemic problems that have resisted easier fixes. You will be trusted with goals that matter at the company level, and judged on outcomes rather than activity.

You will establish and evolve scalable team structures, recognizing when to create a team, when to hire a specialized role, and when teams should combine for a better outcome. You will demonstrate frugality by prioritizing the initiatives that achieve the greatest impact for the least resource, and by driving down the places where the organization applies the same engineering effort year after year. You will retain a strategic focus while staying close enough to the technology to ask the hard questions — where do we bottleneck the business, and should this system continue to exist at all. You will build closed-loop mechanisms that tell you quickly when an initiative is at risk, and act decisively.

Above all, this is a leadership role. You will grow Engineering Managers and senior technical leaders through coaching, strategic project assignment, and genuine delegation of ownership. You will partner with Principal Engineers on the decisions that outlive any single roadmap, give credit visibly, own results in both directions, and build an organization that is better for your presence but does not depend on it.

**Responsibilities**

* **Own the Infrastructure Vision:** Set the long-term technical direction for the Golden Path across cloud platform, build and release, data infrastructure, developer experience, and the AI-enabled software development lifecycle. Make the case for multi-year investment and decide what we improve, invent, deprecate, or simplify.
* **Lead and Develop Leaders:** Manage, coach, and grow a team of Engineering Managers and senior technical leaders, and may directly manage one or two high-impact teams in a critical technology area. Build succession depth, develop and promote top performers, and handle complex people situations with judgment.
* **Design the Organization:** Structure teams to encapsulate technology areas cleanly so that customer, business, and technology needs are met. Recognize when to create a team, when to hire specialized roles, and when teams should combine for a better outcome.
* **Drive Reliability and Deployment Safety:** Reduce the blast radius and duration of production failures for every customer. Hold the organization to incident, time-to-resolution, and availability targets, and establish mechanisms that make regressions visible before they reach production.
* **Own Cost Discipline at Scale:** Shape and execute infrastructure cost-optimization strategy across the organization — setting reduction targets, establishing tracking metrics, forecasting accurately, and evaluating the cost-benefit of new projects and technologies against business objectives.
* **Accelerate Developer Productivity:** Treat internal engineers as customers. Drive build speed and reliability, test infrastructure quality, AI-assisted development adoption, and tooling maturity — and attack recurring operational toil wherever the organization spends the same engineering effort year after year.
* **Communicate Strategically:** Drive high-level written and verbal communication across senior leadership — tenets, architectural plans, planning documents, and business reviews — and input into company-level technical OKR planning.

**Requirements**

* **Strong Technical Background:** 12+ years of software engineering experience with deep infrastructure or platform depth — cloud architecture, distributed systems, build and release engineering, managed data platforms, or large-scale operations.
* **Manager of Managers:** 8+ years of engineering management experience including proven success hiring, developing, and promoting Engineering Managers, and leading senior and staff-level ICs and geographically distributed teams.
* **Infrastructure Platform Ownership:** A track record owning a large, shared technology surface used by other engineering organizations, with demonstrated ability to drive adoption and standards across teams you do not control.
* **Cloud and Cost Fluency:** Strong command of AWS (GCP a plus) and the economics underneath it — commitment and savings-plan strategy, compute elasticity, instance and processor migrations, and cost observability as a first-class architectural concern.
* **Operational Excellence:** Demonstrated ability to set and hit reliability and operational targets at scale, with real experience in incident management, observability, progressive delivery, and root-cause-driven remediation.
* **Comfort with Ambiguity:** A self-starter who can take an undefined business problem and open technology strategy and produce a structured, phased, resourced plan — and who distinguishes clearly between one-way and two-way doors.
* **Security and Compliance Aptitude:** Solid understanding of enterprise security concepts including IAM, zero-trust and service-to-service authorization, least privilege, data isolation, and regula

**Job Description**
-------------------

The Project Manager Operations Consultant/ Circuit Analyst position is responsible for providing technical and administrative support within the Radio Team and in cooperation with the EIS circuit team of a sensitive Federal customer. The role further includes coordinating operations to include order/initiate provisioning, execute decommissioning, and tracking status of the appropriate voice circuits, data circuits, and POTS lines on time and in accordance with customer procedures. * Serve as the primary operational liaison between cross-functional internal teams, external stakeholders, enterprise solution providers, and site vendors (including EIS, OCI, and AT&T) to ensure seamless project alignment and communication.

* Provide comprehensive root-cause analyses and operational overviews during site outages, collaborating directly with AT&T and OCI Field Technicians for rapid issue resolution.
* Proactively align preventive maintenance schedules with AT&T and OCI teams to safeguard mission-critical circuits and minimize operational disruptions.
* Manage the full lifecycle of circuit-related hardware, coordinating delivery, deployment, stage-gate tracking, and reverse logistics in partnership with USSS points of contact (POCs), site leads, and vendor representatives.
* Deliver high-level administrative oversight for newly onboarded circuit sites, facilitating rigorous documentation reviews and securing required approvals from OCI executive leadership.
* Prepare and present weekly executive status dashboards for OCI leadership regarding the RAD initiative, offering detailed breakdowns of outstanding deliverables, TTUs, and site construction timelines.
* Lead coordination for National Special Security Event (NSSE) circuit requests alongside Field Technicians, serving as OCI's principal point of contact for EIS and AT&T during high-priority operations.
* Maintain and continuously audit the global circuit inventory database, collaborating with the CIO, onsite network engineering teams, and EIS to reconcile data gaps and ensure full record integrity.
* Administer and manage telecom circuits for the communications program by processing, auditing, analyzing, organizing, and correcting telecommunications billing; validating discounts; ensuring accurate department billing; monitoring the disconnection of unused lines and circuits; and reporting to the on-site Senior Manager of the Field Service Team.

Amazon's network is a key differentiator for AWS, enabling the global operation of thousands of applications across hundreds of thousands of servers worldwide. We are looking for a Network Development Manager to hire, manage, and develop a team of Network Development Engineers responsible for the end-to-end operational health of the ADC network. You will own capacity management and forecast planning, implementation, automation, change control, process management, and continuous improvement across the classified partitions. You will represent networking to service teams, infrastructure partners, and government stakeholders, ensuring we meet their needs for innovation, delivery, and safe operations in an environment where the margin for error is small and much of the tooling and telemetry commercial teams rely on has to be built.
  
  
At Amazon, we ask our technical leaders to be strong engineers who dive deep and help their engineers make sound decisions and deliver quality solutions. You will maintain a solid technical understanding of routing, switching, optical transport, and network automation, and ensure the right expertise exists on the team. You will also be a thoughtful people manager who mentors your engineers and builds an environment of mutual trust and respect, which matters even more in ADC where teams are smaller, more isolated, and carry a heavier operational load per person. The ideal candidate has a track record of driving operations and continuous improvement for large-scale, mission-critical networks, a passion for operational excellence, and the judgment to safely implement change, measure performance, and respond to events so the network always operates as intended.
  
  
The candidate selected must obtain and maintain a security clearance at the TS/SCI with polygraph level. Upon start, the selected candidate will be sponsored for a commensurate clearance for each government agency for which they perform AWS work.
  
  
Key job responsibilities
  
  

* Own the end-to-end operational health of the ADC network across the classified partitions: availability, performance, change control, and continuous improvement.
* Hire, develop, and retain a team of Network Development Engineers; own onboarding, career growth, 1:1s, and mentoring.
* Run a sustainable on-call rotation that honors SLAs without burning out a small classified-region team.
* Ensure network changes are designed, reviewed, and executed safely at scale under ADC's access and change-control constraints.
* Drive incidents and availability risks to resolution, and own Correction of Error (COE) follow-through so problems do not recur.
* Manage operations with data, metrics, and dashboards; build the monitoring, automation, and tooling ADC has historically lacked.

* Represent networking to service, infrastructure, and government stakeholders so dependencies and deliverables are met.

You lead a team of Network Development Engineers operating AWS's network inside classified regions. A typical day mixes 1:1s and career coaching with reviewing network changes, walking through an incident or COE with an engineer, and unblocking cross-team dependencies. You spend time on the metrics that show where the network and the team need attention, and on the tooling, automation, and monitoring ADC is still building. The Network Engineer II provides day-to-day operational support for the client’s in-scope network, connectivity, wireless, security, optical, voice, and unified communications infrastructure.  **Requirements**  

* Serve as a dedicated Tier 2 network support resource, resolving incidents within documented procedures and escalating complex or high-impact conditions to senior engineering resources.
* Provide operational support for routers, LAN and data center switches, firewalls, load balancers, network access control, WAN edge devices, VPN infrastructure, routing and switching protocols, VLANs, segmentation, QoS, and high-availability configurations.
* Provide hands-on Cisco ACI/APIC operational support, including fabric-health monitoring, fault and event triage, endpoint and EPG troubleshooting, VLAN/VXLAN connectivity. Escalate fabric design or high-risk changes to senior engineers.
* Monitor, investigate, and improve infrastructure availability and performance using health, capacity, telemetry, configuration, threshold, log, interface, latency, jitter, packet-loss, redundancy, and failover indicators where supported.
* Troubleshoot and manage Cisco SD-WAN controllers, edge devices, overlays, tunnels, internet circuits, and site-to-site or remote-access VPN services.
* Support wireless controllers and access-point infrastructure, including availability, registration, RF utilization indicators, authentication failures, roaming, interference, firmware status, configuration backup, security alerts, capacity, and coverage trends.
* Perform alert validation, incident triage, service-restoration actions, incident remediation, problem management, root-cause analysis, post-incident reviews, known-error tracking, and corrective-action follow-up.
* Implement approved standard changes and assist senior engineers with normal or emergency changes, including maintenance-window coordination, validation, rollback execution, closure documentation, and follow-up actions.
* Coordinate OS, firmware, and infrastructure patching activities within the approved scope, including planning, testing, rollout, validation, and vendor coordination.
* Maintain accurate HLD/LLD documentation, logical and physical diagrams, configuration records and backups, SOPs, runbooks, troubleshooting procedures, IPAM/DNS/DHCP records, inventories, monitoring definitions, change logs, and knowledge-base articles.
* Provide technical input for recurring service reviews, including infrastructure health, incident and alert trends, capacity, performance, lifecycle concerns, risks, documentation currency, vendor cases, and continuous-improvement recommendations.

**JOB QUALIFICATION REQUIREMENTS:**

* Minimum of two years of hands-on experience supporting enterprise or public-sector network environments in a managed-services, NOC, infrastructure operations, or similar support model, including practical Cisco ACI/APIC administration or troubleshooting experience.
* Demonstrated troubleshooting experience across routing, switching, firewalls, VPN, wireless, SD-WAN, network segmentation, QoS, high availability, and network performance, with the judgment to escalate issues beyond the role’s level of authority.
* Hands-on Cisco ACI/APIC experience is required, including working knowledge of tenants, application profiles, EPGs, bridge domains, contracts, endpoint learning, fabric health, faults, interface policies, and basic leaf-spine troubleshooting. Experience with Cisco enterprise networking should also include Catalyst switching, ISR/ASR or Catalyst 8000 routing, common routing protocols such as BGP, OSPF, and EIGRP, and switching protocols such as Spanning Tree; Nexus experience is strongly preferred.
* Working knowledge of Palo Alto, Cisco ASA/Firepower, and Meraki security or SD-WAN platforms.
* Experience with enterprise wireless controllers and access points, RF health indicators, authentication, roaming, interference analysis, capacity, coverage, and firmware lifecycle support.
* Strong technical writing skills for diagrams, SOPs, runbooks, RCA/PIR documents, change records, knowledge articles, configuration records, and client-facing updates.
* Ability to work independently in a dedicated client role while collaborating effectively with service-desk, NOC, engineering, service-management, and client teams.
* Ability to participate in after-hours maintenance, major-incident response, or escalation coverage as required by the 24 x 7 service model.
* Must be eligible to work as a US-based iT1 employee and perform services remotely or locally as required.

**PREFERRED CERTIFICATIONS:**

* Cisco CCNP Enterprise or progress toward a current professional-level Cisco certification.
* Cisco Certified Specialist credentials in enterprise core, advanced routing, SD-WAN, wireless, security, or data center technologies.

**REQUIRED CERTIFICATIONS:**

* Cisco CCNA or a comparable current associate-level networking certification, or equivalent expertise demonstrated through at least two years of relevant network support experience, including hands-on Cisco ACI/APIC experience.
* Vendor certifications required to maintain authorized administrative access to assigned platforms, when applicable.

  
**Benefits**  

* Medical, dental, and vision benefits with highly subsidized premiums
* Two weeks paid time off in your first year, with increasing PTO as tenure increases, and most major holidays off
* 401(k) Plan with employer match
* Onsite Fitness Center
* Onsite Monthly Massages

**Job Summary**
Eagle Wireless is seeking a Program Manager to own and drive customer programs through a phase-gate hardware development process — from initial engagement and design through EVT, DVT, PVT, qualification, certification, and ramp to mass production. This role requires hands-on experience managing an engineered hardware product (e.g., a cellular/wireless module, networking device, or IoT end device) through phase-gate NPI to manufacturing release, and comfort coordinating across engineering, supply chain, quality, and external manufacturing partners.
  
  
**Key Duties & Responsibilities**

* Manage customer-facing programs end-to-end: requirements intake, design and engineering coordination, qualification/testing, certification, and transition to volume manufacturing.
* Own program timelines and deliverables, tracking milestones through phase-gate NPI stages (e.g., EVT, DVT, PVT) to mass production, and flagging/resolving risks before they impact schedule.
* Serve as the primary point of contact for assigned customer accounts, managing expectations and communicating status, risks, and changes clearly and proactively.
* Coordinate cross-functionally with engineering, supply chain, quality, and manufacturing (including contract manufacturing partners) to ensure readiness at each program gate.
* Lead and support phase-gate reviews across the NPI process — including PRD sign-off, design reviews (PDR/CDR), DFM/DFT review, pilot build coordination, and manufacturing readiness assessments.
* Manage BOM, ECO, and documentation control processes in coordination with engineering and supply chain teams.
* Track and help drive regulatory and carrier certification requirements (e.g., FCC, PTCRB, carrier certification) to support program milestones.
* Support manufacturing transfer and cutover activities, including coordination between design/engineering sites and manufacturing partners.
* Prepare and present program status reports, timelines, and risk assessments to internal leadership and customers.
* Identify and drive process improvements within the PMO to improve program predictability and delivery.

**Qualifications/Skills/Knowledge**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Supply Chain, Business, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
* 5+ years of experience in program or project management, including 2+ years specifically managing hardware products through phase-gate NPI (EVT/DVT/PVT or equivalent).
* Demonstrated experience managing an engineered hardware product — such as a cellular/wireless module, networking device, or IoT end device — through a phase-gate development cycle to manufacturing release, from concept/design through qualification and into volume production.
* Experience working with contract manufacturers or external manufacturing partners.
* Strong understanding of phase-gate/stage-gate NPI processes (EVT/DVT/PVT or equivalent), BOM/ECO management, DFx (DFM/DFT/DFA), and manufacturing readiness gates.
* Excellent cross-functional coordination skills, with the ability to work across engineering, supply chain, quality, and manufacturing teams.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills, including experience presenting program status to customers and leadership.
* Proficiency with program/project tracking tools (e.g., MS Project, Smartsheet, Jira/Confluence, or similar) and standard office/productivity software.
* Experience in the cellular/IoT module, networking/telecom equipment, automotive electronics, or wireless communications industry.
* Familiarity with regulatory and carrier certification processes
* Experience with ERP systems (e.g., NetSuite) for BOM, inventory, and production tracking.
* Experience managing programs across multiple manufacturing sites or geographies.

Today, Amazon Web Services provides a highly reliable, scalable, low cost infrastructure platform in the cloud that powers hundreds of thousands of businesses in 190 countries around the world. The AWS Cloud infrastructure is built around Regions and Availability Zones. AWS Regions provide multiple, physically separated and isolated Availability Zones connected with low latency, high throughput, and highly redundant networking. These Availability Zones give AWS customers an easier and more effective way to design and operate applications and databases, and they make those systems more highly available, fault tolerant, and scalable than traditional single data center or multi data center infrastructures. Would you like to join the team that plans and delivers the network builds behind that low latency, high throughput, and highly redundant network?
  
  
Global Connectivity Infrastructure Development (GCID) runs a Delivery function that owns the end to end delivery picture across our telecommunication network infrastructure programs. We are looking for a technically strong Technical Infrastructure Program Manager to run a portfolio of network builds from planning through completion. You will prioritize work based on customer needs and target dates, make sure deliverables come together across teams, and build integrated delivery plans that carry each build to handover.
  
  
You will hold the single, trusted view of delivery status across the program, form a clear position on risk and priority, and recommend decisions to leadership. You will own a portfolio of builds, bring teams to one shared view of status, and drive the prioritization decisions and trade-offs that keep delivery on track. You will give confident, data-backed updates to senior leaders and partner across many teams to move work forward.
  
  
You work well in ambiguity. You set up structure, standardize what you can, and improve the process as you go. You communicate clearly in writing and in person, and you hold a portfolio view rather than get pulled into managing every task. If you want to shape how a global infrastructure program delivers, we would like to talk to you.
  
  
Key job responsibilities
  
  

* Own portfolio management across the program, prioritizing builds and reporting integrated status to leadership
* Drive the implementation of large-scale telecommunication infrastructure deployments on a global scale
* Collaborate with stakeholder teams to gather telecommunication infrastructure deployment requirements
* Develop and maintain process documentation
* Program manage from intake, engineering, business development, material acquisition, deployment, and closeout
* Provide deployment support for projects, augmenting the local region TIPM across the globe
* Create and maintain performance dashboards and KPIs to measure program effectiveness
* Drive process improvements through data analysis and stakeholder feedback
* Lead regular executive updates and cross-functional team communications

**Basic Qualifications**

* 5+ years of program management or technical project management experience
* 5+ years of working cross functionally across several teams experience, or a MBA and 5+ years of program or project management experience
* Experience leading and interacting with cross-functional teams
* Knowledge of best practices and emerging technologies, related to infrastructure (i.e. network, data center, hardware, software)
* Experience with varying scenarios of infrastructure builds
* 5+ years of technical infrastructure or program management experience for data center or telecommunications infrastructure
* Excellence in stakeholder management and executive communication

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Construction Management, Electrical, Mechanical, Civil Engineering, or a similar technical discipline
* Experience with Kaizen and Continuous Improvement Process
* Project Management Professional (PMP) certification
* Experience with supplier or vendor relationship management
* Strong understanding of fiber optic and pre-terminated fiber design, construction, and Outside Plant installation
* Knowledge of civil and telecom design requirements for data centers
* Experience developing program KPIs and performance dashboards (PowerBI, Tableau, or QuickSight)
* Proficiency in Salesforce, GIS platforms, and data visualization tools

The Technical Program Manager administers the qualification and validation of new products, and of retrofits and engineering changes to existing parts, for use in large-scale data center environments. The program spans inside plant (ISP) and outside plant (OSP) optical fiber cable, connectivity, and pathway products from candidate identification through validated, released configuration. The position owns the technical content of the program: product selection and evaluation criteria, test methodology, acceptance limits, measurement integrity, and the qualification record that supports product approval and release. The Technical Program Manager serves as the technical interface between design engineering, construction and installation crews, component manufacturers, and test equipment suppliers, and is accountable for validated, documented, and field-reproducible connectivity products on schedule.

**What You’ll Do:**

* **Validation Program Planning and Execution:** Develop and own integrated validation program plans covering both new product introduction and retrofits or engineering changes to existing parts — qualification sequence, entry and exit criteria, material and laboratory dependencies, and decision gates — holding the critical path and driving programs to documented closure.
* **Inside Plant and Outside Plant Infrastructure:** Manage ISP structured cabling across backbone and horizontal distribution, riser and plenum pathways, main and intermediate distribution frames (MDF/IDF), cabinet and rack-mounted patch fields, fiber distribution frames, splice and termination enclosures, cassette-based modular patching, cable tray, basket and innerduct pathway, and firestopping and pathway segregation; and OSP placement across duct bank and conduit, microduct and air-blown fiber, maintenance holes and handholes, aerial and direct-buried routes, building entrance facilities and points of entry (MPOE), transition splice points, armored and dielectric constructions, and environmental and ingress protection at the ISP/OSP demarcation.
* **Fiber Cable, Connectivity, and Termination Scope:** Qualify single-mode (OS2, 9/125 µm) and multimode cable across the full range of standard counts in general industry use, from 24-fiber distribution cable through 3456-fiber high-count backbone, in loose tube, central core, ribbon, rollable ribbon, and 200/250 µm coating designs, evaluating diameter, bend radius, pulling tension, duct fill, and mid-span access against pathway and installation constraints. Own connectivity across LC and LC duplex, MTP/MPO single-row and dual-row arrays (8, 12, 16, and 24 fiber), and very-high-density MMC arrays (16 and 24 fiber), including pinned (male) and unpinned (female) configurations, UPC and APC endface geometries, gender and key orientation, and polarity schemes spanning TIA-568 Method A, B, and C and the conventions applicable to multi-row arrays. Define and validate patch panel, cassette, adapter plate, and shelf configurations for port density, fiber management, bend radius protection, slack storage, labeling access, and serviceability, and evaluate breakout, fanout, harness, trunk, and pigtail assemblies against port mapping and channel performance requirements.
* **Test, Measurement, and Acceptance:** Establish and govern optical test programs — Tier 1 optical loss test set (OLTS) insertion loss and return loss certification, Tier 2 OTDR characterization, bidirectional testing, length and continuity verification, polarity and fitment verification, and endface inspection and cleaning to recognized criteria such as IEC 61300-3-35 — controlling test reference cord (TRC) grade, referencing method, and calibration state so results are repeatable and defensible. Reconcile measured channel performance against design acceptance criteria and transceiver link specifications, and drive corrective action where acceptance limits are not met.
* **Supplier Qualification and Test Equipment Capability:** Lead technical qualification of cable, connectivity, and pathway manufacturers through sample submission, first-article inspection, mechanical and optical evaluation, failure analysis, root cause determination, and corrective action closure, maintaining a defensible qualification record and a clear statement of remaining gaps per supplier. Evaluate, select, and introduce fiber test and inspection platforms end to end, covering technical evaluation against requirements, procurement support, asset control and inventory, calibration and reference cord management, operator training, and fleet distribution to regional field crews.
* **Documentation and Standards:** Produce and sustain installation work instructions, test procedures, golden samples, first-of-kind build documentation, labeling and administration schemes, and as-built records, maintaining them so methods are applied consistently by field crews and subcontractors without procedural drift.
* **Program Governance and Risk Management:** Maintain accurate program status, ownership, target dates, and documented reasons for schedule movement, and produce recurring technical status reporting for client and internal leadership, surfacing aging, blocked, and unassigned work rather than allowing it to persist. Identify technical, schedule, supply chain, and capability risks in advance, quantify impact, drive mitigation to a named owner and committed date, and escalate with a recommendation.
* **Safety and Regulatory Compliance:** Champion a zero-injury culture in laboratory and field environments, ensuring personnel and subcontractors understand and apply laser safety, confined space, excavation, aerial work, and fiber handling requirements, and that work complies with OSHA and other applicable regulations and site access requirements.

At Affirm, we exist for the moments that matter—giving people a clear, predictable way to pay over time, with no hidden fees, no surprises, and no tradeoffs on what matters most.
  
  
As a Senior Technical Account Manager (Senior TAM, L6) at Affirm, you will own the operational aspect of technical account management across Affirm's strategic alliance portfolio—alerting, monitoring, troubleshooting, delivering against SLAs, fielding technical inquiries, and performing investigations and analysis, while also driving technical initiatives that translate merchant business objectives into technical strategies and product optimizations. Senior TAMs are part of the Engineering team and collaborate closely with Affirm's Product, Engineering, Operations, Customer Success, and Frontline Technical Support teams.
  
  
This is an operations-heavy role to start. Expect the majority of your early focus to be on keeping merchant integrations healthy—monitoring, triage, troubleshooting, and SLA delivery—while you progressively take on more custom solutioning and cross-functional initiatives. Over your first 6–12 months, as you build operational mastery, you will grow into owning your own book of accounts and carrying it through to end-to-end account ownership.
  
  
A Senior TAM independently owns operational health across the strategic alliance portfolio, designs custom integration solutions grounded in Affirm's standard integrations, drives cross-team collaboration on initiatives, acts as a technical lead on team projects, and mentors less-experienced members of the team.
  
  
What You'll Do
  
  

* Own the operational aspect of technical account management across Affirm's strategic alliance portfolio—alerting, monitoring, troubleshooting, and fielding technical inquiries—so integrations stay healthy and issues are resolved quickly.
* Deliver against SLAs, proactively surfacing technical risks before they become customer-impacting and responding with urgency to merchant issues.
* Perform in-depth investigations and root-cause analysis across logs, queries, and integration data, owning resolution end to end and escalating to cross-functional partners or executives when needed.
* Drive technical initiatives and partner with internal and merchant stakeholders on launch initiatives—expansions, promotions, new product adoption, and integration optimizations—that grow the value of the accounts after launch.
* Design and deliver high-scope, often-custom integration solutions grounded in Affirm's standard integrations—combining, extending, and tailoring them to complex, open-ended problems while balancing speed, quality, maintainability, reliability, and scalability.
* Act as a technical lead for internal projects, defining and delivering well-scoped milestones and executing the project roadmap.
* Operationalize best practices by creating and updating playbooks, runbooks, alerting, and UAT certification plans across the strategic alliance portfolio and continuously reduce keep-the-lights-on (KTLO) work.
* Partner with Product and Engineering leads to identify, plan, and prioritize projects based on team goals and resources, acting as the voice of the merchant to influence the roadmap.
* Mentor and level up less-experienced TAMs, share learnings from your integrations and investigations, and contribute to interviewing and team development.
* Over your first 6–12 months, grow into owning a dedicated book of strategic alliance accounts—carrying operational ownership through to end-to-end account ownership.

What We Look For
  
  

* Professional Background: at least six years in a technical, external-facing role such as Technical Account Management, Solutions/Partner Engineering, or Solutions Architecture—ideally within FinTech, payments, or SaaS—with a demonstrated track record of owning the operational health of technical accounts and delivering against SLAs.
* Operational Ownership: proven ability to run alerting, monitoring, troubleshooting, and technical inquiries across a set of accounts, balancing reactive operational work with proactive initiatives.
* Ownership & Autonomy: proven ability to independently scope and deliver complex, open-ended technical work, and to partner with stakeholders on launch initiatives, with strong project management and follow-through.
* API Expertise: deep understanding of RESTful APIs, webhooks, and the HTTP protocol, with hands-on experience using tools like Postman to debug and validate integrations.
* Architecture Fluency: Experience in API integrations and the ability to design custom solutions on top of them to solve complex merchant challenges.
* Coding & Code Fluency: ability to read and understand production-level code (HTML, JavaScript, SQL, and ideally one server-side language such as Python) and to author new, novel queries to diagnose merchant or system issues.
* Troubleshooting Acumen: ability to diagnose issues using browser developer consoles, log analysis and observability platforms (e.g., Snowflake, Chronosphere), and ticketing systems (e.g., Jira, Notion).
* Technical Communication: excellent verbal and written communication; able to tailor explanations to both non-technical leaders and technical teams, read a room and adjust in real time, and synthesize technical challenges back to internal teams.
* Relationship Management: ability to discover and develop relationships with technical decision-makers, secure written consensus on integration milestones, and drive cross-team collaboration.
* Leadership & Mentorship: demonstrated ability to mentor teammates, set best practices, and lead technical initiatives; a growth mindset with self-awareness and a habit of seeking and acting on feedback.

Nice to Have
  
  

* Familiarity with the payments ecosystem.
* Familiarity with web/mobile application architecture.
* Experience implementing or customizing e-commerce platforms, payment gateways, or in-store point-of-sale systems.
* Experience acting as a technical lead on cross-functional projects and influencing product roadmaps.

* Lead in-person executive business reviews for strategic customers in your portfolio, including interfacing with C-suite executives and other technical leaders to align to business objectives and agree to a mutual success plan

* Document all customer interactions in internal systems, including Gainsight and Salesforce.com
* Provide feedback and guidance to leadership on key signals within MongoDB Atlas that indicate healthy or unhealthy customer accounts; as our product evolves, we’ll need to be constantly adjusting our engagement strategies based on these signals, which you’ll be in the best position to identify and share back with internal teams
* Manage the relationship with Sales Leadership and Account Executives in your territory, including reporting on business performance, training on best practices, and rolling out program updates to ensure sales people and leaders are abreast of best practices for interacting with Customer Success
* Forecast expected churn and growth to your senior leadership team
* Help interview, onboard and ramp new team members - as a more senior team member you will have an immediate role in who joins the team
* Act as a leader amongst your peers, running enablement sessions, product certifications and being vocal in team meetings to ensure those around you grow

**Where And How You Can Work**
Our flagship office is in Sydney, Australia, but we've made our way from down under, to a campus in Austin, Texas which is now home to our US operations. This is a hybrid role in Austin, Texas, so you must be able to commute to our office 1-2 times a week.
  
  
**About The Team**
Our Sales and Success (GTM) team supports Canva Enterprise, with the mission to empower every organization to design. Canva Enterprise is an AI platform with design and productivity tools that helps organizations securely and easily create, collaborate, and publish high-impact visual content at scale.
  
  
Our Customer Success group is dedicated to delivering value for Canva Enterprise customers post-sale by driving adoption, engagement + growth. The team collaborates closely with cross-functional partners to ensure ongoing customer satisfaction and is responsible for retention, renewals, and revenue growth.
  
  
**About The Role**
As a Strategic Customer Success Manager at Canva, you are a commercially minded, consultative partner to our most valuable customers in North America. You own the full post-implementation journey, guiding customers from kick-off and early adoption all the way through renewal and expansion. This is a strategic, revenue-driving role where you serve as a trusted advisor, helping customers unlock the full value of Canva's platform in service of their most important business priorities.
  
  
You will work closely with Strategic Account Executives, Implementation, Technical Account Managers, Solutions Consultants, Ecosystem Partners and other key stakeholders to deliver seamless customer experiences and maximize account value.
  
  
**What You’ll Do**

* Customer success management: Lead the post-sale relationship of Canva’s strategic accounts within the customer journey, including onboarding, training, adoption, and advocacy.
* Account growth: Proactively identify and work on upsell and cross-sell opportunities in partnership with Sales by deeply understanding customer’s evolving business needs
* Renewals: Own renewal execution and expansion strategy for a strategic book of business, directly contributing to Net Revenue Retention (NRR) and Gross Revenue Retention (GRR) outcomes
* Defend the customer base: Proactively diagnose risk, develop mitigation plans, and mobilize internal resources—including Implementation, Support, and Technical Account Management—to protect and grow accounts before issues escalate.
* Partner cross-functionally across teams to advocate for customer needs, influence product roadmap, and champion best-in-class customer success practices and frameworks

**What We’re Looking For**

* You have a proven track record: 6+ years of Enterprise-level post-sale experience in B2B SaaS with a demonstrated history of exceeding renewal and expansion quotas. You’ve owned a book of business and can speak to your retention and growth results with specificity.
* You are a data-driven storyteller: You use data and analytics to build compelling narratives that influence both customer decision-makers and internal stakeholders. You don’t just report metrics, you interpret them.
* You’re Commercially minded: You think like a business owner. You don’t just manage relationships, you manage revenue. You proactively identify growth levers, negotiate strategically, and aren’t afraid of commercial accountability.
* You’re consultative & strategic: You lead with curiosity. You ask the right questions, connect product value to business outcomes, and position yourself as an indispensable partner rather than a reactive resource.
* You are a relationship builder: You build genuine trust at every level. You’re skilled at multi-threading, navigating complex org structures, and developing executive-level credibility that creates lasting partnerships.
* You communicate effectively and with influence: You communicate with passion and precision. You can rally cross-functional teams, present to executives, and tailor your message to any audience.

**What's in it for you?**
Achieving our crazy big goals motivates us to work hard - and we do - but you'll experience lots of moments of magic, connectivity and fun woven throughout life at Canva, too. We also offer a range of benefits to set you up for every success in and outside of work.

* Equity packages - we want our success to be yours too
* Health benefits plans to support you and your wellbeing
* 401(k) retirement plan with company contribution
* Inclusive parental leave policy that supports all parents & carers
* An annual Vibe & Thrive allowance to support your wellbeing, social connection, office setup & more
* Flexible leave options that empower you to be a force for good, take time to recharge and supports you personally

* Contactless sensing that monitors respiration and motion with medical-grade accuracy
* Native predictive models that detect 85% of preventable adverse events several days in advance
* Enterprise integrations that operationalize predictions directly inside EHR, care-coordination, billing, and compliance workflows

* Renewal forecasting and expansion pipeline, reported weekly
* Churn-risk playbooks: spotting low adoption early and turning it around
* Field feedback to Product, with specific workflow examples

* Experience running executive business reviews and reporting on retention, adoption, or utilization metrics

* Customers on the provider side of healthcare: skilled nursing, home health, hospitals, or post-acute networks

The Sparta Code
  
  
Understanding is non-negotiable
  
  
***Understanding leads to believing. Believing leads to winning.***
The 'why' is the difference between compliance and conviction. Before we execute, we ask: why does this matter, who does it serve, what changes if we win? People who understand the mission don't need to be managed.
  
  
Ask for forgiveness, not for permission
  
  
***Most decisions are reversible. Most fears are not.***
90% of decisions are reversible. Make them, ship, iterate. Perfection is the enemy of efficiency. Bias for action means moving before you have all the answers, but it isn't recklessness. The rule: tell the rest of us what you did, what changed, what you learned.
  
  
Fall in love with the problem
  
  
***The mission wins. Your idea doesn't have to.***
Solutions flatter our ego. They feel like progress. But solutions without problems are opinions, and opinions don't move customers, markets, or teammates. The goal is to find what's true, not to win the room. If your idea gets killed because a better one comes along, that's the system working.
  
  
**It's your fault. Lucky you.**
***If it's on you, it's in your control.***
True ownership sounds harsh until you feel how liberating it is. If every problem is yours, you stop spending energy on who to blame and start spending it on how to fix it. Effective leaders default to 'it's on me'. Not out of guilt, but out of agency.
  
  
Conflict is a gift
  
  
***Honesty is an expression of care.***
Withholding feedback is choosing comfort over growth, yours and your colleague's. Staying silent deprives others of the chance to learn. We challenge openly and with positive intent. Done with care, this builds trust. Done with ego, it destroys it.

* **Drive adoption and value.** Our north star is customers doing real work: someone active in STACK on at least five days in the last 30. Find the accounts that have slipped and help them get back on track with practical, workflow-focused conversations.
* **Manage renewals.** Keep a renewal calendar for your book and start every renewal conversation at least 90 days out. Automated reminders handle the routine work, so you can focus on results.
* **Protect and grow seats.** Help customers keep the users they have and add more as their teams grow. Spot expansion opportunities and pass qualified leads to our sales team.
* **Forecast accurately.** Call commit, risk, and lost renewals by name each week.
* **Be your customers' go-to contact.** Answer workflow questions yourself, bring in Support for product issues, and loop in our Industry Consultants for trade-specific work.
* **Pick up accounts from implementation.** Accounts with two or more users join your book from our Onboarding & Consulting team at day 120.

**About LawnStarter**

LawnStarter is the nation's leading on-demand marketplace for lawn care and outdoor services, spanning three brands: LawnStarter, Lawn Love, and Home Gnome. We've cleared $750M in bookings and turned a profit three years running. Founded in Austin in 2013, we're a team of about 180 that scales past 500 employees during peak season. The marketplace itself is easy to describe and hard to run well: a customer requests a service, we price the job and match it to an eligible Pro, the Pro claims and completes the work, and we process payment and take a commission.

We're entering the most ambitious stretch in the company's history as we build new verticals, new software products, and the groundwork to become a multi-billion-dollar company.

One of our company values is AI or Extinction: every task, AI-first. No exceptions, no excuses. Top 1% or we're already a fossil. This role is hired against that bar.

**The Role**

This is a biz ops generalist role, built for someone who wants to work across many parts of the business instead of owning one narrow lane. You'll start as an individual contributor with no direct reports, in a new seat reporting directly to the COO. Your first owned area will be building Service Delivery into a working operational function. This will entail adding structure, visibility and process to the way we ensure as many customer jobs as possible are completed successfully and on time by LawnStarter Pros, in lawn care and other services we offer now and over time.

New projects will show up unscoped over time. That's by design. As LawnStarter enters new verticals and grows toward a multi-billion-dollar future, big problems will keep surfacing with no obvious owner, and you'll be one of the people the COO trusts to run them down.

**What makes this role different:**

* You work on some of the biggest company-wide projects, cutting across teams and functional areas.
* You'll be a top builder in Brain, LawnStarter's internal AI toolkit built on Claude Code that already powers everything we do across the company: metric queries, document drafting, bug triage, and more. We expect you to approach your work in an AI-first fashion, leveraging Brain to build new systems and processes that will push the limits of how fast AI can accelerate business results. Every project you run is built AI-first: the analysis, the tooling, the process automation, the monitoring. You build it yourself instead of waiting on an analyst or engineer.
* You own outcomes end to end, from recommendation through execution. Strategy without follow-through doesn't count here.

**What You'll Own**

* **Service Delivery, from the ground up.** Despite LawnStarter's considerable scale and reach, Service Delivery doesn't exist yet as a dedicated function. You'll help define the standards we should meet for job completion rates and speed, measure whether we hit them, and design processes, incentives and real-time interventions that get tested with Pros and customers in the field to lift performance. Scope covers every vertical and every delivery model, from today's 1099 Pros to potential W-2 crews under future evaluation.
* **Raising customer & Pro retention rates.** When we deliver service with excellence, Pros and customers alike stay with us longer. Working tightly with peers across Product, Data and Support, you'll identify new opportunities for us to boost retention and LTV and play a key role in driving resulting initiatives cross-functionally.
* **Whatever comes next.** New projects will land on your plate as the company grows into new verticals and builds new software products. You'll take them from "we should look into this" to building and then running systems with structure, KPIs and owners.

**Problems to Solve**

**Build a Service Delivery function that doesn't exist yet.** Right now, no one formally owns whether LawnStarter delivers the service it promises. You'll define the standard for what a Pro should deliver, then build the agents and pipelines that measure adherence to it and run the tests that change behaviors and outcomes in the field.

**Move metrics.** Leverage systems thinking and AI expertise to drive business results that sit across various functional teams. That means untangling handoffs where several teams touch a problem or goal and no one team owns the outcome.

**Take unscoped problems from ideas to fully-running and automated systems.** Some of the most important work here hasn't been named yet. At some point, someone will raise a fuzzy, unframed problem and say it needs attention. Your job is to take that starting point and build whatever tooling or process it needs, at record speed, and hand back something that runs, with a clear owner and quantitative targets attached.

**What Success Looks Like (Year 1)**

* Service Delivery is a working function with a defined (and elevated) service standard, a way to measure adherence to it, clear SOPs, and an intervention and incentive playbook that's been tested and proven to lift results.
* At least one project nobody had scoped a year earlier has gone from "we should look into this" to a heavily-automated, running system with a named owner and tracked KPIs.
* Tools you built with AI are in daily use by people other than you, and the way you work has raised the bar for how the company uses AI.
* The COO can hand you a gray-area problem with no playbook and trust that what comes back is data, a recommendation, and a plan to execute it.

### **About Wellness Equity Alliance**

Wellness Equity Alliance is a national multidisciplinary health organization that designs and delivers integrated, community-based care for populations most impacted by health inequities. We do this through mobile and field-based models, providing medical care, behavioral health services, substance use treatment, harm reduction, and care coordination in nontraditional settings such as encampments, schools, reentry sites, and rural communities, as well as with sovereign tribal nations. Grounded in trauma-informed, culturally responsive, and data-driven practices, WEA combines clinical expertise, lived experience, and advanced population health analytics to reduce barriers to care, improve continuity, and strengthen local systems. We have partnered with more than 60 public agencies, managed care plans, and community-based organizations across the U.S. to implement scalable, sustainable programs that are advancing health equity and improving outcomes for historically marginalized populations.

We are known as Renegades, Rebels, Disruptors and Dreamers. If that sounds like you, we want you on our team.

### **Overview**

Street Medicine provides direct healthcare to unhoused individuals wherever they are, with a strong focus on assessing and responding to their physical, social, and psychological needs.

Enhanced Care Management (ECM) is a statewide Medi-Cal benefit for members with complex needs. Enrolled members receive comprehensive care management from a lead care manager who coordinates all health and health-related care, including physical, mental, and dental care, as well as social services.

Community Supports (CS) are services provided by Medi-Cal managed care plans that address health-related social needs, promoting healthier lives and reducing the need for higher, costlier levels of care.

### **Position Summary**

The Street Medicine Behavioral Health Provider is a licensed or associate clinical social worker who sees patients directly in the field. As a member of WEA's multidisciplinary street medicine team, this provider delivers behavioral health assessment, treatment, and crisis care to unsheltered people experiencing homelessness and others living with serious mental illness (SMI) and substance use disorders (SUD), and carries a caseload of ECM members as their care manager.

This role is 80% field-based and 20% administrative. Field work takes place in encampments, shelters, vehicles, motels, drop-in centers, hospitals, and other community settings alongside WEA's medical providers, nurses, and community health workers. Administrative time covers documentation, care coordination, case conferences, and training.

The provider reports to the Director of Behavioral Health.

**Location:** Southern California, with field work in Los Angeles, San Bernardino, San Diego, and the Coachella Valley.

**Position type:** Full-time, hourly, or per diem.

### **Key Responsibilities**

**Direct Patient Care (Field)**

* See patients directly in the field as part of street medicine rounds, building trust with people who have often been failed by health systems.
* Conduct biopsychosocial and mental health assessments, including suicide and violence risk assessment, and make diagnoses within the provider's scope of practice and license.
* Provide brief and ongoing therapeutic interventions, including motivational interviewing, cognitive behavioral approaches, trauma-informed care, and harm reduction counseling.
* Provide crisis intervention, including de-escalation, safety planning, and coordination of emergency and psychiatric care when needed.
* Screen for and support substance use treatment, including linkage to medication for addiction treatment with WEA's medical providers.
* Support medication adherence and provide psychoeducation to patients and their support networks.
* Provide telehealth follow-up when in-person contact is not possible.

**Enhanced Care Management**

* Serve as lead care manager for an assigned caseload of ECM members, especially those with SMI or SUD and those experiencing homelessness.
* Outreach to and engage referred members, explain ECM services, and enroll members who agree to participate.
* Complete ECM assessments and develop, update, and carry out person-centered care plans that integrate behavioral health, medical, social, and housing needs.
* Coordinate care across medical, behavioral health, substance use, and social services, and close the loop on every referral.
* Make sure each member has an assigned primary care provider and support engagement with that provider.
* Support members through transitions of care, including discharges from hospitals, psychiatric facilities, and jails.
* Connect members to housing, sobering centers, substance use treatment, Community Supports, benefits, and other community resources.

**Team Collaboration**

* Serve as the behavioral health consultant to WEA's street medicine and ECM teams.
* Participate in case conferences and systematic case reviews with the multidisciplinary team.
* Work with external partners, including managed care plans, county behavioral health, shelters, hospitals, and community-based organizations.
* Provide or facilitate training for team members on behavioral health, crisis intervention, and trauma-informed care.
* Contribute to protocols, workflows, and best practices for behavioral health in street medicine.

**Documentation and Compliance (Administrative)**

* Complete timely, accurate documentation of assessments, care plans, treatment, and care coordination in the electronic health record.
* Ensure documentation supports Medi-Cal billing and meets ECM, managed care plan, and WEA standards.
* Report on patient progress and outcomes as required by contracts and WEA leadership.
* Comply with Medi-Cal, CalAIM, HIPAA, and Board of Behavioral Sciences requirements.
* Participate in quality improvement initiatives.

### **Work Environment**

This position is 80% field-based and 20% administrative. Field work takes place outdoors and in street-based settings, encampments, shelters, and community sites, in all weather conditions, with regular travel across the region.

Employment is contingent on successful completion of a background check following a conditional offer of employment and on meeting WEA's Occupational Health Clearance requirements. **Introduction**

Build a more connected world by transforming the customer experience and helping customers transition to modern products and technologies. Our Product teams help shape the future of connectivity by simplifying platforms, improving operations, and delivering solutions that meet evolving customer needs. In this role, you’ll lead strategic wireline transformation initiatives that retire legacy voice products, platforms, services, technologies, and processes. Your work will help protect service continuity, improve the migration experience, reduce operational complexity, and advance the business toward its target end state.

**Job overview**

As a Lead Product Manager for Wireline Transformation and Legacy Product Retirement, you’ll define and execute transformation roadmaps, develop product-sunset strategies, evaluate customer and business impacts, and coordinate customer migrations to target products and technologies.

You’ll partner closely with customer-care call centers and teams across network, engineering, operations, sales, marketing, finance, legal, regulatory, and corporate communications. Together, you’ll plan operational readiness, prepare customer-care representatives, develop internal and customer-facing communications, monitor performance, and establish feedback loops that support a consistent customer experience throughout each transition.

**What you’ll do**

* **Lead transformation and product-retirement strategy:** Define and communicate the wireline transformation strategy, roadmap, measurable outcomes, sunset milestones, dependencies, decision points, and readiness criteria for legacy products, platforms, technologies, services, and processes.
* **Plan customer migrations:** Segment affected customers, establish migration strategies, and define paths to target end-state products or technologies while managing customer retention, service continuity, and escalation risks.
* **Develop business cases and impact assessments:** Analyze customer, revenue, cost, network, operational, and state and federal regulatory impacts; create business cases supporting product retirement, platform simplification, and customer migration.
* **Prepare customer-care operations:** Partner with call-center leaders on contact-demand forecasting, staffing considerations, call-flow planning, operational readiness, and escalation paths. Coordinate agent procedures, training, product-transition guidance, knowledge articles, frequently asked questions, call scripts, and job aids.
* **Coordinate communications and technical execution:** Develop internal and customer-facing communication plans with customer care, marketing, sales, legal, regulatory, corporate communications, engineering, network, and other stakeholders. Address technical dependencies and decommissioning requirements while keeping representatives informed about milestones, offers, migration options, policy changes, and known issues.
* **Manage governance, risk, and performance:** Lead cross-functional governance, resolve escalations, and manage risks involving billing, ordering, revenue, service continuity, operational readiness, customer migration, and escalation resolution. Track and report migration progress, customer retention, contact volume, customer sentiment, cost savings, and decommissioning progress to senior leadership.

**What you’ll need**

* **Product-sunset and migration planning:** Experience building and executing complex product-retirement, customer-migration, or technology-transformation plans.
* **Wireline and telecommunications knowledge:** Understanding of wireline products, network technologies, service delivery, and related operational processes.
* **Business-case and roadmap development:** Ability to develop business cases, prioritize initiatives, define roadmaps, and establish measurable milestones and readiness criteria.
* **Data analysis:** Ability to interpret customer, financial, revenue, cost, operational, network, and product-performance data and translate findings into recommendations.
* **Contact-center operational planning:** Experience supporting demand forecasting, call-flow planning, workforce considerations, knowledge management, training, communications, and escalation processes.
* **Risk and dependency management:** Ability to manage cross-functional dependencies and risks involving service continuity, customer migration, billing, ordering, revenue, operational readiness, and platform decommissioning.

**What you’ll bring**

* **Education or equivalent experience:** Bachelor’s degree or equivalent relevant experience.
* **Relevant experience:** Approximately 5–8 years of product management, business transformation, telecommunications, or related experience.
* **Transformation leadership:** Experience managing complex product-sunset, customer-migration, or technology-transformation initiatives.
* **Customer-care partnership:** Experience partnering with customer-care or contact-center organizations on operational planning, training, and communications.
* **Cross-functional leadership:** Strong communication, presentation, negotiation, and stakeholder-management skills, with demonstrated success managing competing priorities, dependencies, risks, escalations, and senior-leadership updates.
* **Preferred experience:** Knowledge of consumer wireline products, customer lifecycle management, service migrations, or transformation programs. Familiarity with call-center operations, workforce planning, knowledge management, agent training, and contact-volume forecasting is preferred, along with experience creating customer communications, agent scripts, frequently asked questions, job aids, and escalation procedures.

Help shape the future of wireline connectivity by making complex transitions easier for customers and the teams that support them. You’ll have the opportunity to lead high-impact transformation programs, collaborate across the organization, and deliver measurable improvements in customer experience, operational efficiency, and platform simplification.

Customer Experience

* Establish and maintain rigorous QA standards across the editorial production lifecycle.

We have an immediate opening for **Field Technician I** **.** Responsible for asset management: processes deliveries and replenishes consumables as well as coordinates shipping and receiving of materials. We are hiring an HR Automation Engineer to design, build, automate, operate, and continuously improve the applications, integrations, data solutions, and AI capabilities that power HR automation and digital experiences at Lumen.

  

This is a senior hands-on engineering role responsible for delivering solutions across Power Platform, Microsoft Fabric, Azure application development, AI platforms, and enterprise integrations. The role partners closely with HR leaders, analysts, product owners, and engineers to transform business needs into secure, scalable, and supportable solutions.

  

In one sentence: engineer the applications, automations, integrations, and AI-powered experiences that transform manual HR processes into modern digital services.

**The Main Responsibilities**
-----------------------------

**Workflow Automation & Robotic Process Automation**

Design, build and support end-to-end automated workflows in Power Automate, spanning Microsoft 365, SuccessFactors, ServiceNow and our HR data sources, replacing manual and ticket-driven HR processes.

Build and maintain robotic process automations for systems that lack modern integration capabilities, including exception handling, credential management, monitoring, and operational support.

Implement logging, alerting, retry mechanisms, and operational monitoring to ensure solutions are reliable, supportable, and scalable.

Identify opportunities to eliminate manual effort while balancing automation benefits with long-term maintainability and business value.

**Apps, Data & Semantic Modeling**

Develop Power Apps solutions, canvas and model-driven, together with the Dataverse data models and security roles behind them, giving HR practitioners and employees a governed front door to those processes.

Design, develop, and support custom applications when business requirements extend beyond low-code platforms.

Build secure web applications, APIs, and services using Azure App Services, Azure Functions, Azure Storage, and related Azure technologies.

Develop APIs and reusable services that enable integration between HR applications, automation platforms, analytics solutions, and AI agents.

Implement application monitoring, telemetry, performance optimization, and operational support practices using Azure-native tools and Application Insights.

Evaluate whether requirements are best addressed through Power Platform, custom application development, vendor capabilities, analytics solutions, process redesign, or other approaches.

**Agent Development & Analytics**

Build and extend agents in Microsoft Copilot Studio, including topics, actions, knowledge sources and connected agent patterns, and wire automation actions into the conversational HR experience the team is standing up.

Develop Fabric data agents grounded on curated semantic models, so HR questions are answered from governed data rather than from spreadsheets.

Deliver Power BI content on top of those models, including DAX measures, row-level security and report designs that HR leaders and COE partners actually use.

**Integration & Platform Lifecycle**

Build custom connectors and API integrations using REST, OAuth 2.0 and OData where out-of-the-box connectors fall short, including authentication, throttling and pagination handling.

Own application lifecycle management for the platform: solution-based deployments, environment strategy, source control and automated pipelines from development through production.

Manage the maintenance work that keeps the estate healthy, including connector and gateway updates, credential and certificate rotation, deprecation handling and post-change validation.

**Governance, Enablement & Delivery**

Establish and enforce platform governance, including environment and licensing standards, naming and reuse conventions, and monitoring through the Power Platform admin center.

Create reusable components, templates and patterns that let the wider HR team build safely, and coach analysts and citizen developers on using them.

Work with product managers, analysts, and stakeholders to evaluate, prioritize, and deliver automation and AI opportunities in short, visible increments.

Produce architecture diagrams, solution documentation and run books so automations are supportable by the team rather than by a single builder.

Communicate effectively with technical and business stakeholders and recommend solution approaches that balance business value, user experience, maintainability, and long-term supportability.
